title: Rapid Mixing of Parallel Kac's Walk: From Spheres to Stiefel Manifolds
authors: Qian Chen, Minglong Qin, Fang Song, Penghui Yao, Mingnan Zhao
abstract: Kac's walk is a classical local random walk whose action on a single real unit vector in dimension $d$ mixes in total variation in $Θ(d\log d)$ sequential steps~\cite{PS17}. Lu, Qin, Song, Yao, and Zhao introduced a parallel version of Kac's walk that mixes a single quantum state in $O(\log d)$ rounds~\cite{LQSY+26}. After discretizing the randomness and replacing it by suitable pseudorandom primitives, this parallel walk gives rise to pseudorandom state scramblers, and was subsequently shown to yield pseudorandom unitaries~\cite{LQSY+25}.   We study what happens when the parallel Kac's walk acts simultaneously on $k$ orthonormal quantum states. We prove that, for any $1\leq k < d$, after $O\!\left((k+\log d)\log(d/\varepsilon)\right)$ steps, the joint distribution of the $k$ output states is $\varepsilon$-close, in both Wasserstein and total variation distance, to that obtained by applying a common Haar-random unitary to the same inputs. This generalizes the dispersing property of the parallel Kac's walk from a single quantum state to multiple orthonormal quantum states. Equivalently, viewing an ordered collection of $k$ orthonormal states as a point on the complex Stiefel manifold $V_{d,k}=\{X\in\mathbb C^{d\times k}:X^\dagger X=I_k\}$, we show that the parallel Kac's walk mixes rapidly on $V_{d,k}$, with both Wasserstein and total variation mixing times bounded by $O\!\left((k+\log d)\log(d/\varepsilon)\right)$. This extends the Wasserstein mixing result of Pillai, Smith, and Vaikuntanathan for the standard Kac's walk on real Stiefel manifolds~\cite{PSV26}.
summary: This work analyzes the mixing rate of a parallel version of Kac's walk when applied to multiple orthonormal quantum states, modeling the system on the complex Stiefel manifold. The authors prove that the mixing time is bounded by $O((k + \log d) \log(d/\epsilon))$ in both Wasserstein and total variation metrics. This result generalizes previous findings by showing rapid scrambling for multiple entangled quantum states.
main_problem: The paper investigates the rate at which the parallel Kac's walk mixes when acting simultaneously on $k$ orthonormal quantum states.
main_result: The joint distribution of the $k$ output states mixes rapidly on the complex Stiefel manifold $V_{d,k}$ in $O((k + \log d) \log(d/\epsilon))$ steps for both Wasserstein and total variation distances.
method: The proof utilizes coupling techniques and detailed analysis of the Jacobian of the evolution map to bound the distance between the walk's distribution and the Haar-random unitary distribution.
model_or_system: The system is the parallel Kac's walk, viewed as a Markov chain on the complex Stiefel manifold $V_{d,k}$, representing an ordered collection of $k$ orthonormal quantum states in $\mathbb{C}^d$.
key_observables: Joint distribution of $k$ output states, Wasserstein distance ($W_D$), and total variation distance ($\epsilon$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on constructing explicit couplings and establishing contraction estimates for the distance metrics on the Stiefel manifold.
paper_structure: The paper develops the analysis by first establishing Wasserstein mixing bounds using contraction estimates, followed by constructing a coupling argument to prove the total variation mixing time.
why_interesting: The rapid mixing property of quantum random walks on structured manifolds like the Stiefel manifold is crucial for understanding quantum scrambling and the efficiency of quantum information processing protocols.
